• Synonym: Liobagrus xiurenensis

There are three species in this genus: X. dorsalis, X. xiurenensis and X. gigas.
Asia: China, Zhujiang River. The specific name xiurenensis refers to the Xiuren River, Pearl River drainage, Guangxi Province, China, the type locality.

Description: Elongated body, round in the front and gradually flattened towards the back, covered by a membrane. Short dorsal fin; very small eyes covered by a skin membrane. Dorsal spines (total): 1; dorsal soft rays (total): 6; anal soft rays: 7–8; vertebrae: 41–44. Dorsal-fin rays i,6; anal-fin rays vi,8 to vi,11; pectoral-fin rays i,6 to i,7; pelvic-fin rays i,6.

Colouration: The edges of the dorsal, anal and caudal fins are yellowish; the back is brownish and the belly yellowish.

IUCN Red List: assessed as Data Deficient, as the species is not well known beyond its type locality. Potential threats include overfishing and pollution.

Devi, R. & Boguskaya, N. 2009. Xiurenbagrus xiurenensis. The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species 2009. Froese, R. and D. Pauly. Editors. 2009. FishBase. www.fishbase.org, version (01/2011). The ETYFish Project Fish Name Etymology Database © Christopher Scharpf.
